Europe runs on three overlapping clubs: the EU, the euro and NATO. Their join dates show who came when, and who stayed out.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The EU, per this map: six founders joined in 1958. Denmark, Ireland and the UK followed in 1973, Greece in 1981, Spain and Portugal in 1986. Data: Wikipedia (Oct 2026).
2/ Then came Austria, Finland and Sweden in 1995, and the big wave of 2004 across Central and Eastern Europe. The UK shows in red: it joined in 1973 and left on 31 January 2020.

3/ The euro is a smaller club. It launched in 1999 as an accounting currency with 11 countries; coins and notes arrived on 1 January 2002. Greece joined in 2001, Slovenia in 2007. Data: Wikipedia (Oct 2026).
4/ Bulgaria became the 21st EU member to adopt the euro on 1 January 2026. Sweden, Poland and Hungary are in the EU but keep their own currencies. Montenegro and Kosovo use the euro unilaterally.

5/ NATO is a different map. Twelve countries founded it in 1949, Greece and Turkey joined in 1952, West Germany in 1955 and Spain in 1982. Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024. Data: Wikipedia (Oct 2026).
Three clubs, three maps. Some countries sit in all three, others in only one or none. Which European country do you think belongs to the fewest? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
